title: Graded-uniform Hom divisibility for finite near-projective modules
statement: Let $R_0$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $K_0\subseteq R_0$ an ideal. Write $\operatorname{gr}_K(R)=\bigoplus_{j\geq0}K^j/K^{j+1}$ with graded multiplication [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. There exist integers $D,q\geq0$, depending only on the degree-preserving unital ring isomorphism class of $\operatorname{gr}_{K_0}(R_0)$, with the following property. Let $R$ be any Noetherian commutative ring, $K\subseteq R$ an ideal, and suppose $\operatorname{gr}_K(R)\cong\operatorname{gr}_{K_0}(R_0)$ by a degree-preserving unital ring isomorphism. Let integers $n\geq c\geq0$ satisfy $n\geq\max(q+(D+1)c,(D+2)c)$ and, if $D=0$, also $n\geq q+2c$. Put $A=R/K^n$, $t=n-(D+1)c$, and $w=n-(D+2)c$. Let $M$ be a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] such that for every $a\in K^c$ there are an integer $r_a\geq0$ and $A$-linear maps $f_a:M\to A^{\oplus r_a}$ and $g_a:A^{\oplus r_a}\to M$ with $g_af_a=\bar a\operatorname{id}_M$, where $\bar a$ is the image of $a$ in $A$. For every $A$-linear map $u:M\to K^n/K^{2n}$ there exist a finite set $J$, elements $a_j\in K^c$, and $A$-linear maps $\psi_j:M\to K^w/K^{n+w}$ such that $p u=\sum_{j\in J}\mu_{a_j}\psi_j$. Here $p:K^n/K^{2n}\to K^t/K^{n+t}$ sends $x\bmod K^{2n}$ to $x\bmod K^{n+t}$, and $\mu_a:K^w/K^{n+w}\to K^t/K^{n+t}$ sends $y\bmod K^{n+w}$ to $ay\bmod K^{n+t}$. All quotient modules have the $A$-action induced by multiplication in $R$. No completeness assumption on $R$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0GAC (lemma-factor-hom), with the graded-isomorphism invariance of its constants in Tag 0GA6 (section-uniform); the (A,n,c)-module condition is written as its finite-free factorization condition, more-algebra.tex Tags 0G92 (lemma-near-projective), 0G93 (definition-near-projective).

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-blowup-uniform-tensor-section-bound] to the fixed graded ring and choose its $d\geq1,q\geq0$; set $D=d$. These constants work simultaneously for every $(R,K)$ in the statement. If $n=0$, then $A=R/R=0$, so $M=0$ and the assertion holds with $J=\varnothing$. Hence assume $n\geq1$ and use $Y_n,\mathcal L_n,s_n,P_n$ of the cited node. The hypotheses give $w=n-(D+2)c\geq0$, $t=w+c\geq q$, and $n-2c\geq q+(D-1)c$. $A$ is Noetherian: every ideal lifts to a finitely generated ideal of $R$. Put $N=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,A)$. By [lem-per-near-projective-dual-comparison], $N$ is finite and has the same scalar-factorization property. Apply its comparison on $Z=Y_n$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$: write $F=P_n(N)$, $P=P_n(M)$, $G=\mathcal Hom(P,\mathcal O_{Y_n})$, and $\alpha:F\to G$. Its kernel and cokernel are killed by $(K^c/K^n)\mathcal O_{Y_n}=\operatorname{im}(s_n^{\otimes c})$.

source.place: 0GA6 and 0GAB; choice of invariant constants and dual module

proof.text: The annihilation hypotheses just verified permit [lem-per-line-twist-double-annihilator-reverse], with the invertible module $\mathcal L_n$ and its map $s_n$. Obtain $\beta_n:G(n)\to F(n-2c)$ satisfying $\alpha(n-2c)\beta_n=\delta_{2c}$. The given $u$ defines $\chi:P\to\mathcal L_n^{\otimes n}$ by pulling back $u$ and multiplying the ideal representatives. Equivalently it defines $\sigma\in\Gamma(Y_n,G(n))$: locally trivialize the line module and regard $\chi$ as a functional; changing trivializations multiplies the functional by the inverse change of basis, so these local tensors glue. Let $\sigma'=\Gamma(\beta_n)(\sigma)$. For each $z\in M$, evaluation gives $e_z(\sigma)=\theta_{n,n}(u(z))$ and $e_z(\alpha(n-2c)\sigma')=\delta_{2c}\theta_{n,n}(u(z))$. Indeed the comparison formula in [lem-per-near-projective-dual-comparison] is $(b\otimes\lambda)(1\otimes z)=b\lambda(z)$, so comparison commutes with evaluation, including all twists.

source.place: 0GAC: sigma, sigma-prime, and the omitted factorization; 0GAB evaluation

proof.text:
Apply the tensor-section bound of [lem-per-blowup-uniform-tensor-section-bound] to $N$ with starting twist $r=n-2c$. Its numerical hypothesis holds by Step 1, and $r-(D-1)c=t$. Thus the image of $\sigma'$ in $\Gamma(Y_n,F(t))$ is $\eta_{N,t}(\tau)$ for some $\tau\in K^t\otimes_R N$. Since $t=w+c$, every coefficient of a finite tensor expression for $\tau$ is a finite sum of products from $K^cK^w=K^t$. Expanding these sums writes $\tau=\sum_{j\in J}a_j\tau_j$ for a finite set $J$, $a_j\in K^c$, and $\tau_j\in K^w\otimes_R N$. For an expression $\tau_j=\sum_l b_{jl}\otimes\lambda_{jl}$ define
$$\psi_j(z)=\sum_l b_{jl}\widetilde{\lambda_{jl}(z)}\pmod {K^{n+w}},\qquad z\in M,$$
where $\widetilde{\lambda_{jl}(z)}$ is any lift from $A$ to $R$. Changing a lift changes the answer by $K^wK^n$; bilinearity of this formula makes it independent of the tensor expression and $A$-linear. Its values lie in $K^w/K^{n+w}$. This is a concrete construction of all required maps.

source.place: 0GAA parts (4)-(5), followed by 0GAC: tensor coefficient decomposition and evaluation

proof.text:
Fix $z\in M$. Evaluate the equality $\delta_{(D-1)c}(\sigma')=\eta_{N,t}(\sum_j a_j\tau_j)$ and then apply $\alpha(t)$. Step 2 and the local formula for evaluation give
$$\delta_{(D+1)c}\theta_{n,n}(u(z))=\theta_{n,t}\Bigl(\sum_j\mu_{a_j}\psi_j(z)\Bigr).$$
On the right, a tensor $a_jb_{jl}\otimes\lambda_{jl}$ evaluates to $a_jb_{jl}\widetilde{\lambda_{jl}(z)}$ modulo $K^{n+t}$. On the left, the compatibility of $\theta$ with decreasing twists in [lem-per-blowup-uniform-tensor-section-bound] identifies the result with $\theta_{n,t}(p u(z))$. Since $t\geq q$, $\theta_{n,t}$ is injective, so $p u(z)=\sum_j\mu_{a_j}\psi_j(z)$. This holds for every $z$. Finally $t=w+c$ shows $a_jK^{n+w}\subseteq K^{n+t}$, verifying the stated multiplication maps, and $0\leq t\leq n$ verifies the quotient map $p$. Thus the equality is exactly in the quotient modules in the statement, with their $A$-actions.
